schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE DETERMINISTIC JUDGE AN EXTRACTION IS GRADED BY, and nothing else. Two checks, each a PROOF RECORD: ``inspect_record_shape`` (the candidate carries exactly CANDIDATE_FIELDS, a non-empty what and why, at least one anchor, and a ``read`` string even when empty — five lanes) and ``inspect_anchors_verbatim`` (one lane carrying its POPULATION: every anchor the draft claims as EXPECTED, the ones actually found in the source as ACTUAL). ``record_shape`` and ``anchors_verbatim`` survive as VIEWS over them — DERIVED, NEVER PARALLEL — and ``findings_of`` is the ONE reading of 'did a lane fail'. ``normalized`` is the single whitespace ruler both the anchor compare and the device's source floor measure with. No parsing, no prompt, no device, no digest: those are the extraction's, not the judgment's.
why: THE CARVE-OUT WAS FORCED BY A MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-13, and that is the whole why. The device's charter always said the same two things — the DRAFT comes from an oracle through a caller-injected seam, and the JUDGMENT is deterministic, 'never by CC's opinion, the least independent witness'. Both halves lived in one component, survivable only because nothing could SEE the second half. Converting the checks onto the shared proof record (ruling everything-always-proved-and-listing-what-it-proved) made them import cairn.tools.gate, and bin/cmd/determinism — which reads gate-ness as a DIRECT-import fact — immediately reported what had been true since the device was built: VIOLATION, gate via extractor.py, REACHES AN ORACLE via live.py. The instrument was right and was not softened. A gate may not have an oracle at fire time OR at sleep, because a component holding both is one refactor away from a judge that consults the thing it is judging.

feedback.why: THE JUDGE INSPECTS A DRAFT IT DID NOT WRITE. Its one finding is every_anchor_appears_verbatim_in_the_source: an anchor the draft claims to have taken from the source and that is not in the source. Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. The upstream creative entity is the drafting step, and the drafting step is an ORACLE reached through a caller-injected seam that the holding device owns — the judge deliberately holds no oracle at all, which is why it was carved out on 2026-08-13 in the first place. So the only address that can act on a fabricated anchor is the device that owns the seam, the prompt and the model behind it: cairn/devices/intention_extractor. Routing to the judge itself would be routing a hallucination to the detector that already caught it — the 'improve the generator' half of Akien's bound is the half that pays here, because the inspector did its job.

invoke: `from cairn.devices.intention_extractor.machines.judge.judge import INSPECTORS, findings_of` — `INSPECTORS[name](draft, source)` returns that check's proof record; `findings_of(record)` returns the findings to refuse with. The device holds it and re-exports the names as its published surface; nothing else imports it.
node_class: code-seam — the judgment is the code, one address. Held by cairn/devices/intention_extractor at devices/<device>/machines/<name>/, the shape CLAUDE.md names for a device's held machines and the shape the builder already uses eight times.
entry: CARVED OUT of cairn/devices/intention_extractor/extractor.py on 2026-08-13 — a move, not a fresh build: the checks, their provenance docstrings and their teeth came across whole, and their conversion to the proof record happened in the same voyage. In-house precedent composed, cited not copied: the builder is PURE DETERMINISTIC while holding eight gate machines, and skills/chart keeps its sleep seam while its gates berth as machines. Both answered this question the same way before it was asked here.
state_and_history: None of its own. A judgment is a pure function of (draft, source); the crossing it grades is the DEVICE's breadcrumb, and the extraction's disposition is the caller's. A machine that started keeping a tally of what it had judged would be keeping the device's state at the wrong address.
gates: IT IS THE GATE. Each check returns a proof record — one entry per lane that RAN, EXPECTED beside ACTUAL, passes included — and the refusal is the == compare over it, per entry, with no oracle anywhere near it. THE ATTRIBUTION LANE IS GUARDED: a draft whose ``anchors`` is not a list has nothing to walk, so that lane is ABSENT rather than green, and ``the_draft_is_anchored_at_all`` has already refused. A CHECK THAT DID NOT RUN IS ABSENT, NOT PASSED, so one fault never multiplies into findings in two vocabularies.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) this module importing anything but ``cairn.tools.gate`` — the carve-out is worth nothing if the import surface widens, and its proof measures this rather than asserting it; (2) a check defined here AND in the device — a fork is the carve-out undone; (3) a view (``record_shape``, ``anchors_verbatim``) growing an implementation of its own instead of reading its inspector's mismatches; (4) a lane whose EXPECTED and ACTUAL cannot be == when it passes — such a lane reds on every healthy draft and measures nothing (caught twice on 2026-08-13, in this component's own conversion); (5) a lane that refuses while naming no finding being DROPPED rather than named — ``findings_of`` is not a filter over the findings lists alone; (6) a check landing here without a dated caught failure in its docstring — a check nobody was taught by.
horizon: Valid while the extraction contract holds: anchors are verbatim quotes and inference goes under ``read``. A new check joins by being a caught failure first (Law 1), and the registry is pinned by the proof, so adding one means editing the tooth that names them.
how_it_learns: IT DOESN'T, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN — it is the independent witness, so a judge that learned from the drafts it grades would stop being independent of them. What learns is the RULESET, and it learns by correction: a bad extraction a check could have caught becomes a check, dated and provenance-carried, and the class stops recurring. The learning loop runs through the humans and the ticket, not through this module's runtime.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — an anchor is the measurement of an attribution), Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics: the checks refuse, they do not advise), and Law 9 (red is the default; a draft is refused until it earns its pass).
owner: the intention_extractor device (a machine has users, and here it has exactly one holder).
proof: proofs/test_judge.py — five teeth, including the import-surface measurement that is this machine's reason to exist.
provenance: Ruling 2026-08-13-everything-always-proved-and-listing-what-it-proved (the conversion) plus the bin/cmd/determinism violation it surfaced (the carve-out). Founding failure the checks themselves answer: 2026-07-26, 'the graph type is a coordinate, not a class' recorded as Akien's ruling when it was CC's inference.
learns: Yes; it learns from verdicts on judgment accuracy — each verdict is a labeled training pair.
